I am a housing lawyer. u/grasshoppa1 is correct. When you make a maintenance request, the owner or their agent has a reasonable belief that the need for entry is acknowledged by the tenant. They can not enter, say, a month later, nor can they use entry to do work that isnt necessary, but if they are examining or repairing someone the tenant has called to their attention, provided they are entering in a reasonable timeframe, you have no recourse. 

Legally speaking, your right to sold occupancy is called "quiet enjoyment." This term is often confused to mean silence or noise levels, but the term "quiet" in real estate means "without another person on entity with a claim to the title." Since your lease (and state law) require the landlord to give 24 hour notice of nonemergency entry, this applies to any matter that you have not requested -or- is requested but a delayed response. 

Your remedy if the landlord repeatedly enters without notice in non requested, non emergency matters is being allowed to break your lease and move elsewhere. There is no legal process in which you would recover money. The only extant one is you can get an injunction that serves as a court order the landlord must abide by the lease terms. This is pointless and expensive. 

But here, I hate to say it, is you being upset for nothing. If you want them to give notice prior to entry, then make requests for maintenance in writing and request notice of entry prior to doing so. But frankly, any legal action if they do not would almost assuredly be futile.

No offense taken, for full disclosure I'm a straight white man so can only speak of the experiences of my friends and family. 

Edit: it's also really healthy to be able to have open frank discussions about these issues. 

You are correct that most people don't care about a person's sexuality, but it is part of daily life. As a man friends will talk about women, the 'default' is to attract women, etc. Coming out allows you to tell people that "hey for me it's about men. I want to attract men". As a straight man it means I can now treat my gay friends equally because we can talk about boys instead of girls. I suppose that's one aspect, I imagine there is a lot more than just sexual attraction. That is just an example. 

Coming out isn't a celebration, I think it has that image thanks to TV or films, from what I understand it's more of a release of pressure. It's like having a secret that you can finally tell, it's more a out being honest with yourself than it is anyone else patting you on the back. 

I think you're confusing acknowledgment with special treatment. People acknowledge that you are straight on a daily basis through conversation and observance, when someone comes out it means that you can now acknowledge them for who they are instead of assuming they are something else. 

As a woman do you want people to acknowledge the struggle that women have in society? It's the same thing. 

Your point a out it being confusing for people who aren't 'different' is super super valid. There is lots of discussion about men struggling to deal with their masculinity for that very reason and in fact in the UK one of the most disadvantaged groups of people are the poor white male youth, they've been labelled as 'forgotten' people by some social studies. But that's a different kettle of fish. 

I agree life would be a lot better if we accepted everyone and stopped labelling so much, but unfortunately right now we're a long way off. In the same way that women are persecuted the world over, so are gay people. That's why for the time being there is still some gravitas to 'coming out'.
